app.title: LoVPN
nav.label: Sections
rail.note: Local only. No account, no cloud, no telemetry.
noscript: LoVPN needs JavaScript to run its window. Use the lovpn command instead.
ring.label: Protection: {headline}. {checks}
head.protected.title: You’re protected
head.protected.body: Connected. Every check below was observed on this computer.
head.protected.bodyTo: Connected to {profile}. Every check below was observed on this computer.
head.degraded.title: Not fully protected
head.degraded.body: You asked to be connected, but at least one check is failing. Details below.
head.degraded.bodyTo: You asked to be connected to {profile}, but at least one check is failing. Details below.
head.connecting.title: Connecting…
head.connecting.body: Waiting for the first reply from your server.
head.blocked.title: Internet is blocked
head.blocked.body: The kill switch is holding traffic back on purpose. Connect again, or restore normal internet.
head.disconnected.title: Not connected
head.disconnected.body: Your traffic goes out normally. Nothing is blocked.
head.unknown.title: Can’t tell yet
head.unknown.body: LoVPN could not observe everything it needs, so it will not claim you are protected.
explain.vpn.ok: The tunnel is up, the server answered recently, and your traffic is routed into it.
explain.vpn.fail: The tunnel is not working as expected. Traffic may not be using it.
explain.vpn.unknown: LoVPN could not inspect the tunnel, so it will not claim it works.
explain.dns.ok: Name lookups go to your server’s resolver. Lookups to other servers outside the tunnel are blocked.
explain.dns.fail: Name lookups may reach servers outside the tunnel.
explain.dns.unknown: LoVPN could not inspect DNS settings, so it will not claim they are safe.
explain.dns.none: DNS is not changed while you are disconnected.
explain.ipv6.ok: IPv6 traffic is blocked so it cannot bypass the IPv4 tunnel.
explain.ipv6.fail: IPv6 traffic may still leave your device outside the tunnel.
explain.ipv6.unknown: LoVPN could not inspect the IPv6 block, so it will not claim it is in place.
explain.ipv6.none: IPv6 is not changed while you are disconnected.
explain.kill.ok: If the tunnel drops, other traffic stays blocked until it returns.
explain.kill.fail: The kill switch is missing or altered. If the tunnel drops, traffic could leave unprotected.
explain.kill.unknown: LoVPN could not inspect the kill switch, so it will not claim it is armed.
explain.kill.off: This server’s profile has the kill switch turned off. If the tunnel drops, traffic goes out unprotected.
explain.kill.none: Not armed while you are disconnected.
explain.kill.blocking: Your connection is blocked on purpose until you connect or restore normal networking.
copy.manual: Select the text and copy it yourself
copy.label: Text to copy
error.title: That didn’t work
restore.title: Restore normal internet?
restore.body: This turns the kill switch off. Your traffic will go out without the tunnel until you connect again.
svc.title: The LoVPN service isn’t running
svc.body: The window can only show and change things through that service, so it can’t tell you anything yet. {hint}
svc.hint.windows: Open Services, find “LoVPN Client” and start it. If it is missing, run the LoVPN installer again.
svc.hint.linux: Run: sudo systemctl start lovpn-clientd. If the unit is missing, run the LoVPN installer again.
which.title: Which server?
which.body: Choose where to connect. You can set a default on the Servers page.
home.welcome.lead: Your own VPN, on your own server. Nothing leaves this computer except traffic to the server you choose.
tech.none: No tunnel checks while you are disconnected.
onb.title: Set up your first server
onb.lead: LoVPN connects to a server you run yourself. There is no account to create. Here is what happens:
onb.1: Name the server and create a key for this device.
onb.2: Send the public part of that key to whoever runs the server.
onb.3: Import the profile file they send back, and the server’s key they give you separately.
onb.5: See what was actually verified on the Privacy page.
servers.title: Servers
servers.lead: A server is one place you can connect to, with a key made for this device.
servers.mode.strict: Strict kill switch: traffic stays blocked until you restore it
servers.check.title: Profile check
servers.check.intact: The stored profile is intact and this version of LoVPN supports it. Reachability is not tested here: a VPN server stays silent to strangers, so only connecting proves it.
servers.remove.title: Remove {name}?
servers.remove.body: This deletes the profile and this device’s key for it. To use this server again you will need a new profile from its administrator.
wiz.name.title: Name this server
wiz.name.label: Name
wiz.name.hint: Lowercase letters, digits, - and _ (for example: home). It is only a label on this device.
wiz.name.invalid: Use 1–32 lowercase letters, digits, - or _, starting with a letter or digit.
wiz.key.title: Create a key for this device
wiz.key.body.windows: Your device needs its own key. The secret half stays inside the LoVPN service and is never shown. You send only the public half.
wiz.key.body.linux: Your device needs its own key. The secret half stays in a private file only until the service stores it. You send only the public half.
wiz.key.send: Send this public key to whoever runs your server. It is safe to share.
wiz.key.have: I already made a key for this name
wiz.profile.title: Add the server’s profile
wiz.profile.keyhint: Get this from your administrator by a different route than the profile (a call, a chat). LoVPN refuses the profile if the key it names is different: that is how a tampered profile is caught.
wiz.done.title: Server added
wiz.done.body: The profile matches the key you entered and is stored. Connect to see whether everything checks out.
devices.title: Devices
devices.lead: This computer has its own key for each server. Other devices are added on the server itself.
devices.none: No servers yet, so this device has no keys.
devices.other.title: Adding or removing other devices
devices.other.body: Whoever runs the server manages its devices with {create}, {revoke} and {rotate}. A revoked device stops connecting right away.
privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.lead: A check is marked verified only when LoVPN observed it on this computer just now.
privacy.not.title: What this program does not do
privacy.telemetry.d: This build has no code that reports usage, crashes or settings to anyone.
privacy.account.d: There is nothing to sign up for, and no LoVPN cloud.
privacy.network.d: It talks to the LoVPN service on this computer. Only the service contacts your server.
privacy.dnsnote: DNS is verified as resolver settings plus a firewall rule, not by sending test lookups.
diag.title: Diagnostics
diag.lead: What the service sees right now. Nothing here contacts any outside server.
diag.note: The copy leaves out profile names, server addresses, keys, tunnel addresses and file paths.
settings.title: Settings
settings.lead: Only settings that do something are listed here.
lang.note: Messages written by the service itself, and technical codes, stay in English.
notify.label: Tell me when my protection changes
notify.hint: Only while this window is open and in the background. Messages never contain server names, addresses or keys. For notifications while the window is closed, run lovpn-tray.
notify.denied: Your browser or system blocked notifications for this window. Allow them in its site settings to use this.
notify.unsupported: This window cannot show notifications on your system.
settings.default.label: Used when you press Connect
settings.default.hint: You can’t change the default while connected. Disconnect first, or connect to another server from the Servers page.
settings.kill.title: Kill switch and other protections
settings.kill.body: These come from each server’s profile, so they can’t be changed from this window. Ask your server’s administrator for a profile with a different kill switch.
settings.about.body: LoVPN, free and self-hosted. Local only: no account, no cloud, no telemetry. Licensed MIT.
logs.title: Logs
logs.lead: Events from the LoVPN service. They never contain keys or traffic.
logs.label: Service log
logs.empty: The service has not logged anything yet.
adv.title: Advanced
adv.lead: Tools for when something looks wrong. The Home page is enough for daily use.
adv.reconnect.d: Rebuild the tunnel. The kill switch stays on while it happens.
adv.repair.d: Re-apply routes, DNS and firewall rules if a check is failing.
adv.reset.d: Disconnect, turn the kill switch off and restore normal internet. Your servers and keys are kept.
adv.reset.title: Reset networking?
adv.reset.body: Your traffic will go out without any protection until you connect again.
adv.todo.ipv6.d: IPv6 is blocked instead, so it can’t leak.
adv.todo.split.d: All traffic goes through the tunnel.
adv.todo.lan.d: Local devices such as printers are unreachable while the tunnel is up.
note.title: LoVPN
note.degraded: Protection is incomplete. Open LoVPN for details.
note.blocked: Internet is blocked on purpose by the kill switch.
note.unknown: LoVPN can’t verify your protection right now.
note.disconnected: Disconnected. Your traffic goes out normally.
err.window.closed: The LoVPN window lost contact with the program that runs it. Close this window and start LoVPN again.
err.window.bad-reply: The window got an unreadable reply. Close it and start LoVPN again.
err.service.unreachable: The LoVPN service is not running, or you are not allowed to use it. Nothing was changed.
